messages.subject: How to import an audio file on R and use the function "env"?

Hi,

I'm just a begginer with the package Seewave and R in general.

I try to compute the th index of an audio .wav file. To do this, I have to use the function env.

But when I lauch my script, R crash when the env function is started. I don't really understand why. I think it's because the format of the object that I use in the function is not suitable: indeed, the format of my object is "Large wave" (that I obtain with the function "ReadWave"). I tried to use the function env with an audio file from seewave (obtained with "data(tico)") and that works (the format of "tico" is "formal class wave" and not "Large wave").

Do I use the wrong function to import my audio file on R? If it's the case, how can I do to import it?

Thank you for you help!

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] How to import an audio file on R and use the function "env"?
parts:
Hi Jérémy,

It's hard to say what the maximum file size must be. It depends on the file and on your computer.

To analyze in sections, you could cut it into smaller waves (using the cutw() function or an external program).

Also consider down-sampling. To me, it looks like your file has a really high sampling rate. Depending on what you're trying to analyze, you might be able to get away with a lower sampling rate. To down-sample, take a look at the reamp() function and try something like this, where 'g' is the new sampling frequency.

wave_small <- resamp(wave, g = 44100, output = "Wave")

Once, again, though, the approach you take depends on what you're trying to do with the results. I'm not familiar with the th index, so I can't help you out much there.

Good luck!

Steffi

Dr. Stefanie LaZerte
Biologist, R and CitSci Enthusiast
